clues: This startup built an architecture that treats higher-dimensional tensor contraction as its native hardware computational unit.
Its second-generation accelerator is a 180-watt, air-cooled card designed for AI inference rather than training.
The Export-Import Bank of Korea made this firm its first direct startup investment since the bank's founding.
Its advisory roster includes a former vice president and general manager for Asia Pacific Enterprise Business at Nvidia.
Led by South Korea's National Growth Fund with a $280 million commitment, its Series D round raised $620 million at a $2.9B valuation.
This Seoul-based startup makes the RNGD inference chip and secured South Korea's largest funding round for a domestic AI chip startup.
